_about: Supplemental map for src/Tools/apidocs/generate_rest_api.py and generate_postman.py. OpenAPI carries no response schemas, so each route's response type, status codes, and notes live here. tags orders and describes the folders and sections. bodies holds an example request body per schema (Postman variables in {{braces}}). examples holds response examples per type, and routeExamples holds one for a single route where the type example does not fit (it wins over examples). samples gives the values the Markdown shows for each {{variable}}. pathVariables names the Postman variable for a path parameter where the default rule (topics/{id} gives topicId) does not fit. parameters notes query values. captures (a "json:" path stores the value as JSON text), postmanQuery, postmanBodies (Postman-only bodies; a string is sent as is), postmanAuth, variableDefaults, firstInFolder, lastInFolder, cleanupFolder (every delete, run after the resource folders), and finalFolder (logout and restart, run last) shape the Postman collection so a run from top to bottom works on a fresh stack and leaves the administrator's password alone. tags.Health: An anonymous liveness and readiness probe. Container healthchecks and load balancers call it.
tags.Server: Public client configuration that the dashboard and mobile app read before anyone signs in: feature flags, the minimum app version, legal links, and the MCP URL.
tags.Token: Sessions. POST /v1.0/token exchanges login headers (an email and password, or an access key and secret) for a bearer token. The other routes validate, describe, refresh, and revoke the token you already hold.
tags.Profile: The signed-in user's own profile and password. Any authenticated user may call these for themselves.
tags.Tenants: Control plane. Tenants isolate every record in the system. Global administrators manage all tenants; tenant administrators can read their own.
tags.Users: Control plane. Users inside a tenant, with their administrator flags. Passwords are write-only.
tags.Credentials: Control plane. Access keys for programs. The secret is returned once, when the credential is created. The auth mode decides how a credential may be used: direct headers, signed requests, session exchange, or a mix.
tags.Roles: Control plane. Built-in and tenant-defined roles. A role is a named set of permissions.
tags.Permissions: Control plane. Permissions (resource types and operations, permit or deny) and the effective permissions a user or credential ends up with.
tags.Assignments: Control plane. Role assignments for users and scope assignments for credentials, at tenant or resource scope.
tags.Audit: Security and administration events: sign-ins, denials, credential use, settings changes, vault reveals.
tags.Request History: Captured REST requests with headers and bodies, for troubleshooting. Retention is set by RequestHistory.RetentionDays.
tags.Settings: Server settings. Secrets come back masked as ******** and a masked or empty secret is left unchanged on update. Some settings take effect only after a restart.
tags.Vault: Encrypted storage for API keys and tokens that model endpoints, search providers, and voices use. Lists and reads never include the secret; reveal is limited to the credential's creator and administrators, rate limited, and audited.
tags.Models: Model endpoints (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, xAI, Ollama, compatible servers, and the agent CLIs in the server image: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Mux), task role assignments, and the accounting record of every model call.
tags.Setup: What the workspace still needs before people can use it (a chat model with a working key, and web search; embeddings and email are optional) and live checks that prove it. Until every required check is Ready, refinement sessions and research requests answer 409 SetupRequired. Options lists the model providers and how each signs in; connect stores the sign-in and points the chat tasks at the endpoint. Verify, options, connect, and model-key are for administrators.
tags.Usage: Model usage and cost, grouped or bucketed over time. Members see their own; administrators can see the tenant, and global administrators every tenant.
tags.Devices: Push notification devices registered by the mobile app for the signed-in user.
tags.Notifications: The signed-in user's notifications. Preferences are one matrix: each kind of notification (run results, briefing ready, audio ready, run failed, plan limit reached, prediction due) on each channel (email, push to a registered phone or tablet, and the in-app list). Without a saved choice, email is on for run results, ready briefings, failed runs, and plan limits, and everything else is off. The in-app list holds the notifications for kinds turned on for that channel; they are kept for 90 days. A topic's email-on-run switch and an edition's email and push switches still apply on top of these preferences.
tags.Topics: The things a reader follows. A topic has a research brief, weighted dimensions, constraints (keywords, domains, feeds, tracked questions), and email recipients.
tags.Refinement: The topic wizard. A session proposes dimensions, asks clarifying questions, drafts the brief and constraints, suggests sources, and then applies the topic. Generating steps call the configured model.
tags.Requests: One-time research requests: a report, podcast, or email summary produced once, now or at a set time. A request can later become a recurring topic.
tags.Schedules: When topics, editions, and requests run. Interval, days-of-week, days-of-month, one-time, and cron schedules, each in a time zone. Preview validates a schedule and lists its next runs.
tags.Runs: Research runs and their stages, cost, search queries, search results, and model calls. Every run and every stage carries its estimated cost; see [Run and stage cost](#run-and-stage-cost). A run can be watched live over server-sent events, canceled, or retried from a later stage.
tags.Search: Search providers (SearXNG, Tavily, You.com, RSS, Hacker News, arXiv, hosted model web search), per-topic provider choices, and test tools for queries and page fetches.
tags.Findings: Ranked results from runs, each backed by evidence. Findings can be pinned or hidden.
tags.Sources: Pages the pipeline fetched for your topics, with their extracted text.
tags.Predictions: Forecasts the pipeline extracted, with confidence and a horizon. They are resolved by hand or by accepting a proposed review.
tags.Suggestions: Things worth digging into next, with a status you move through (accept, snooze, dismiss, done).
tags.Briefings: Composed briefings with sections and items, their Markdown and HTML files, pinning past retention, and regeneration.
tags.Artifacts: Stored files: briefing Markdown and HTML, audio, and exports. Content streams with Range support.
tags.Editions: Recurring briefings that gather several topics, with a template, audio and email switches, and a lookback window.
tags.Templates: Briefing templates in Markdown. Every save is a version; templates can be validated, previewed, rolled back, reset, imported, and exported.
tags.Media: Audio episodes made from briefings, with chapters.
tags.Voices: Text-to-speech voice profiles, with a test route that speaks a sample. Two more routes let anyone who can edit a topic choose its voice: one lists the voices a topic can use (the voice profiles, then the speech server's own voices with readable labels), and one speaks a short preview.
tags.Podcast feeds: Private podcast feed tokens. The feed URL embeds the secret, which is shown once.
tags.Sharing: Public share links for a briefing. One share yields one link to a single page where anyone can listen to the briefing and read it with no sign-in. A share is made on purpose, never by default, always expires (1 to 14 days, 7 when not chosen), and can be revoked. The links are returned once; only a hash of the secret is stored. `sharing.enabled` turns the feature off for the whole server.
tags.Email: The email outbox, test and preview sends, resends, and the signed-in user's email preferences.
tags.Feedback: Ratings and reasons on findings, predictions, suggestions, sources, domains, and briefings. Feedback drives learning and analytics.
tags.Learning: Preferences learned from feedback (or written by hand), their review flow, and ranking weight recommendations.
tags.Analytics: Reports over relevance, accuracy, feedback, suggestions, reasons, quality, email, and runs. Defaults to the caller's data for the last 90 days.
tags.Prompts: Prompt templates by key and scope, topic overrides, version history, rollback, reset, and the prompt lab.
tags.Promotional codes: Global administrators create, generate, and manage promotional codes that grant plans.
tags.Plans: Global administrators manage plans, their entitlement values, and per-user plan assignments.
tags.Account: Sign-up, email verification, password reset, the signed-in user's plan, usage meter, data export, account deletion, and promotional code redemption.
tags.Public: Routes reached from emails, podcast apps, and shared briefing links. They take no session; a token in the path is the credential. Feedback and unsubscribe pages are HTML forms. Shared briefing pages are server-rendered HTML with no script and no cookies.
tags.OpenAPI: The OpenAPI 3 document and Swagger UI that Watson serves. They are not tagged in the document itself.
tags.MCP servers: Remote MCP tool servers that agentic research may call, their discovered tools, and the per-tool allow-list.
tags.Catalog: System-wide publications and private subscriptions. Shared content is generated once; subscription and personal topic limits are separate.
tags.Catalog administration: Global administrators manage canonical publications, research, schedules, and lifecycle revisions. Tenant administrators cannot publish.
tags.Billing: Account-bound Stripe checkout and native Apple/Google verification. A redirect never grants access; verified provider state determines benefits.
tags.Billing callbacks: Provider-authenticated callbacks. Ordinary bearer sessions do not authorize these routes.
tags.Account providers: Account-private encrypted model and speech connections, validation and explicit BYOK funding. No secret is returned.

GET /v1.0/api/briefings/{id}/download.notes: Query `format` is `md` (default) or `html`. The file is sent as an attachment and honors `Range`.

GET /v1.0/api/artifacts/{id}/content.notes: Streams the stored file with its own content type. Pass `download=true` for an attachment. Honors `Range`.

status.200: The token was already registered; the existing device is returned
OK; count is how many were marked

GET /v1.0/public/feedback/{token}.notes: Renders the feedback page from an email rating link. The optional `a` query value preselects an action, and the page asks the reader to confirm it with one button; opening the link records nothing, so mail scanners that follow links cannot rate.

POST /v1.0/public/feedback/{token}.notes: Form post (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) from the feedback page.

POST /v1.0/public/unsubscribe/{token}.notes: Form post (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) from the unsubscribe page.

status.503: The database is unreachable; the body still describes each component.

POST /v1.0/api/topics/{id}/learn.notes: Runs the learning pass at once and returns how many preferences it proposed plus the topic's preferences.

GET /v1.0/api/analytics/runs.notes: Dry runs are excluded and days are gap-filled. Sources examined are the Search stage's items out, fetched are the Fetch stage's items out, and used are the distinct sources behind a non-duplicate finding at or above the display threshold. Provider yield is the share of a provider's results whose source produced such a finding in the same run. Stage percentiles interpolate linearly over finished (succeeded or failed) stage rows.

GET /v1.0/api/voices/available.notes: The workspace's active voice profiles come first (the default one at the top), then the voices the speech server offers that no profile uses yet. The server's list is read from the speech endpoint's `/audio/voices` (Kokoro-FastAPI) and kept for five minutes; `listed` is false when the endpoint has no listing, and the configured default voices are offered instead. `label` is readable where the ID follows Kokoro's naming (`af_heart` is Heart, American English, female) and is the ID otherwise. To use a voice for a topic, send its `voiceProfileId`, or its `voice` when it has no profile yet, in `PUT /v1.0/api/topics/{id}`; the server then reuses or creates the voice profile. Needs permission to read topics.

POST /v1.0/api/voices/preview.notes: Send `voice` (a speech server voice from the available list) or `voiceProfileId` (a voice profile, spoken with its own endpoint, model, and speed). `text` is cut to 300 characters; without it a default sentence is spoken. Each user may ask for 20 previews a minute. 400 when neither is given or the speech server does not offer the voice, 404 for an unknown voice profile, 409 when speech is turned off on the server, 502 `TtsError` when the speech endpoint fails. Needs permission to edit topics.

GET /v1.0/api/briefings/{id}/shares.notes: The owner of the briefing and tenant administrators can list its shares. `tokenHash` is always `redacted`, and the links themselves are never returned here. A share works while `revokedUtc` is null and `expiresUtc` is in the future. `viewCount` and `lastViewedUtc` say whether a link was opened; nothing else about visitors is recorded.

POST /v1.0/api/briefings/{id}/shares.notes: The body is optional. `expiresInDays` must be from 1 to the server maximum (`sharing.maxExpiryDays`, 14 by default); omitted, it is `sharing.defaultExpiryDays` (7 by default, never more than the maximum). A value outside the range is refused with 400 `ValidationFailed`, with `minimum` and `maximum` in `details`; the server never adjusts it silently, and there is no share without an expiry. `showOwnerName` (default false) shows the sharing user's display name on the public pages; the email address is never shown. `readUrl`, `listenUrl`, and `secret` are returned only in this response.

DELETE /v1.0/api/briefings/{id}/shares/{.notes: Revokes a live share; its link answers 404 at once. Revoking twice is harmless. `purge=true` deletes a share that is already revoked or expired, and is ignored for a live one (which is revoked instead).

GET /v1.0/public/shares/{token}.notes: The shared briefing page, for listening and reading: title, topic or edition name, date, a native audio player with chapter links when the briefing has finished audio (each chapter link reloads the page with `t`; a request with `t` is not counted as a new opening), then the briefing rendered from Markdown (raw HTML in the content is shown as text, and outbound links carry `rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"`), and an invitation to sign up. No authentication, no cookies, no script. Sent with `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, and a Content-Security-Policy that allows only same-origin images and audio. An unknown, revoked, or expired link, a deleted briefing or user, and a server with sharing turned off all get the same 404 page. Each successful open adds one to the share's `viewCount`.

GET /v1.0/public/shares/{token}/listen.notes: The address earlier shares used for a separate listening page. It now renders the same single page as `GET /v1.0/public/shares/{token}`, with the same headers and the same 404, so those links keep working.

GET /v1.0/public/shares/{token}/markdown.notes: The briefing text as a Markdown file (`text/markdown`, sent as an attachment named after the briefing title). No authentication. Not counted as an opening. Same 404 as the page for a link that does not work.

GET /v1.0/public/shares/{token}/audio/{f.notes: The audio behind the shared briefing page. No authentication. Honors `Range`. The file name is for the browser and may be anything, for example `briefing.mp3`. 404 when the link does not work or the briefing has no finished audio.

PUT /v1.0/api/model-endpoints/{id}.notes: A null or absent property is left unchanged. To set an optional value back to null, list its name in `clearFields`, for example `{"clearFields": ["temperature", "contextLength"]}`. Names that can be cleared: `endpoint`, `credentialId`, `authMethod`, `model`, `embeddingModel`, `temperature`, `reasoningEffort`, `contextLength`, `inputCostPerMTok`, `outputCostPerMTok`, `cachedInputCostPerMTok`, `cacheWriteCostPerMTok`. Any other name, or a name that the same request also gives a value, returns 400 `ValidationFailed`. The usual rules still apply after clearing (an OpenAI-compatible endpoint needs a URL, a chat endpoint needs a model).

GET /v1.0/api/runs.notes: `sortBy=estimatedCostUsd` lists the most expensive runs first (runs with no priced cost sort last) and `sortBy=durationMs` the longest; `queuedUtc`, `completedUtc`, `createdUtc` (the default), `lastUpdateUtc`, and `status` also work.

status.202: Accepted (the body is an ErrorResponse-shaped notice with error Accepted)

GET /v1.0/api/server-info.notes: Everyone signed in gets the product, version, start time, and uptime. The database type, schema version, pgvector flag, .NET runtime, operating system, pending restarts, and bundled tool links (Grafana, Prometheus, Tempo, Loki) are returned only to global administrators.

status.409: The email matches accounts in several tenants; the body is a TenantSelectionResponse. Sign in again with x-tenant-guid.

status.200: OK (the topic already had this constraint; it is returned unchanged)

GET /v1.0/api/usage/report.notes: With `groupBy=Model` each row is one endpoint and model name: `key` is the endpoint ID and the model name joined by `|`, and `modelEndpointId` and `model` carry the two parts, so the same model name served by two endpoints is reported as two rows.

GET /v1.0/api/usage/timeseries.notes: Each bucket's own fields cover every call in the bucket. With `groupBy`, `groups` lists the range totals per group (highest cost first, limited to `top`, the remainder under the key `(other)`) and each bucket's `rows` holds one row per group that had calls in that bucket, in the same order. `groupBy=Day` returns 400.

PUT /v1.0/api/vault/credentials/{id}.notes: A null or absent property is left unchanged, and a new `secret` rotates the stored value. To remove an optional value, list its name in `clearFields`, for example `{"clearFields": ["expiresUtc"]}`. Names that can be cleared: `headerName`, `username`, `description`, `expiresUtc`. Any other name, or a name that the same request also gives a value, returns 400 `ValidationFailed`, as does clearing `headerName` on a `CustomHeader` secret or `username` on a `BasicAuth` secret.

POST /v1.0/api/vault/credentials/{id}/re.notes: Allowed for the user who created the credential (`createdByUserId`) and for administrators. Anyone else in the tenant gets 403, and a credential in another tenant is 404. Every reveal writes a `CredentialRevealed` audit event.

GET /openapi.json.notes: The OpenAPI 3 document this reference is generated from.

status.202: Accepted (same body whether or not the email has an account)

status.400: LinkUsed (already used: the address is confirmed, so sign in), LinkExpired, LinkInvalid, BadRequest
ValidationFailed (weak password), LinkUsed, LinkExpired, LinkInvalid, BadRequest

status.200: OK (success false with the error when the server cannot be reached)

GET /v1.0/api/setup.notes: Reads the stored state. The only provider call is the optional speech check, for administrators: one short speech request to the configured endpoint, at most once every five minutes. `canConfigure` is true for global and tenant administrators, who also get the optional checks: `embeddings`, `email`, and `speech` (Ready when speech is on and the endpoint returned audio, Missing when it is turned off, Failed with the reason when the endpoint did not answer; it carries the endpoint host in `resourceName`, `model`, and the default `voice`).

POST /v1.0/api/setup/verify.notes: Calls the providers: a short probe prompt per chat endpoint, a test query per default web search provider, one embedding request, and one short speech request. Each endpoint's `lastValidationSucceeded` records the outcome. `check=Speech` (or `Model`, `Search`, `Embeddings`) re-checks only that kind and reports the others from stored results.

GET /v1.0/api/setup/options.notes: Makes no provider calls. Lists the hosted APIs (`Api`: Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, xAI, Ollama Cloud), the agent CLIs in the server image (`AgentCli`: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Mux), and self-hosted servers (`SelfHosted`: Ollama, OpenAI-compatible), with their sign-in methods, recommended first; Anthropic is the recommended provider. For an agent CLI, `installed` says whether the executable is in the server image and `available` is false (with `unavailableReason`) when it is missing or when `Models.AllowAgentClis` is off (`turnedOff` true), as on the hosted service. The example shows four of the eleven providers.

POST /v1.0/api/setup/connect.notes: `authMethod` defaults to the provider's recommended method. `secret` is an API key, a token from `claude setup-token` (Claude Code), or the contents of a sign-in file (Codex `~/.codex/auth.json`, Gemini CLI `~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json`, Mux `~/.mux/endpoints.json`); it is not needed for `ServerSignIn` and `None`, or when the endpoint already has one for the same method. Reuses the workspace's endpoint for the provider (or `modelEndpointId`), or creates one; stores the secret encrypted in the vault; checks it with a live call; and assigns every chat task to the endpoint. When the workspace already has a working model, the new sign-in is tested first and the working one is kept if the test fails. `connection` on the returned status reports the outcome: `succeeded`, `keptPrevious` (true when the working model stayed in use), and `message` (the test result or the provider's error). The secret is never returned. 400 `ValidationFailed`, with `details.field` naming the request field (`provider`, `authMethod`, `secret`, `model`, or `baseUrl`), for a missing provider, model, or secret, a method the provider does not accept, a secret that does not look right (such as an Anthropic API key sent as a setup-token token), or an agent CLI that is turned off or not installed.

POST /v1.0/api/setup/model-key.notes: Stores the key encrypted in the vault (a new credential, or the endpoint's existing one updated), attaches it to the endpoint, and checks it with a live call. The key is never returned. 400 `ValidationFailed` when a value is missing or the endpoint uses the hosted service's key.

cleanupFolder.name: Cleanup
cleanupFolder.description: Every delete in the API, collected here so a run of the whole collection creates and uses each record before deleting it. The folders are undone in reverse order (the newest records first, the tenant and user created earlier last). Bulk deletes remove every matching record, not only the ones this collection made.

finalFolder.name: Run last
finalFolder.description: Requests that end the session or the server. Delete my account is refused for the protected administrator. Logout revokes the token every other request uses. Restart uses the administration key and takes the server down for a few seconds.
